Java's default trust store includes roots that signed weak eMudhra intermediates, so a Java client could be fooled when it connects out. Keycloak has no way out: only the internal networks auth-front (Traefik) and db-auth (postgres-auth), whose certificates come from AetherSpark's own CA, and its database client checks against that root only. Red Hat marks it won't fix; the Keycloak base moves only with Ostium's next notice (D-008; O-035 and O-047 list it).

Uncontrolled memory allocation when guava's compact maps are deserialized. Keycloak reads requests as JSON and forms; Java serialization happens only between cluster nodes, and AetherSpark's Keycloak runs as one node with cache=local (no cluster port). Fixed in guava 33.7.2, not yet in a Keycloak release Ostium has noticed (O-035, O-047).
